cls: Parathyroid hormone analogue - anabolic osteoporosis agent
quick: Not affected by food - subcutaneous injection
Not recommended; not indicated in women of childbearing potential without contraception
Use with caution; not recommended in severe renal impairment
No specific data; use with caution
Heavy alcohol use is a risk factor for osteoporosis; no specific drug interaction
Serum and urinary calcium; orthostatic vitals after first doses
summary: Recombinant human parathyroid hormone (teriparatide, the 1-34 N-terminal fragment of endogenous PTH) is an anabolic agent for osteoporosis. Given once daily by subcutaneous injection, intermittent PTH exposure stimulates new bone formation by preferentially activating osteoblasts, increasing bone mineral density and reducing fracture risk. The main metabolic hazard is hypercalcemia, and transient orthostatic hypotension can occur after early doses. The full recombinant human PTH(1-84) (Natpara/Preotact) is used for hypoparathyroidism but carries an osteosarcoma boxed warning; teriparatide is the widely used PTH analogue for osteoporosis and is the basis of this record.
indications: Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture
Increase of bone mass in men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis at high risk of fracture
Treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in patients at high risk of fracture

dosage.d: 20 mcg subcutaneously once daily into the thigh or abdominal wall
dosage.n: Total treatment duration generally limited to 24 months over a lifetime

dosage.d: 20 mcg SC once daily with caution
dosage.n: Not recommended in severe renal impairment

dosage.d: Initiate 50 mcg SC once daily, titrate per calcium (separate product)
dosage.n: Different product (rhPTH 1-84) with an osteosarcoma boxed warning - specialist use only

admin: Inject subcutaneously into the thigh or abdominal wall once daily
Administer the first several doses where the patient can sit or lie down in case of orthostatic hypotension
Store the pen device refrigerated and use within the labeled in-use period
Rotate injection sites and use proper aseptic injection technique
Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake during therapy
moa: Teriparatide is the biologically active 1-34 fragment of human parathyroid hormone. Once-daily (intermittent) administration stimulates osteoblastic bone formation more than bone resorption, increasing trabecular and cortical bone mass and improving bone microarchitecture and strength. This anabolic action contrasts with the catabolic effect of continuously elevated endogenous PTH (as in hyperparathyroidism).

absolute: Metabolic bone diseases other than primary osteoporosis (including hyperparathyroidism and Paget disease)
Prior external-beam or implant radiation therapy of the skeleton
Bone metastases or history of skeletal malignancy
relative: Concurrent digoxin therapy (hypercalcemia predisposes to toxicity)
monitor: Orthostatic blood pressure after early doses

preg: Teriparatide is not recommended in pregnancy and is not indicated in women of childbearing potential. If pregnancy occurs, discontinue. There are no adequate human data and animal studies showed skeletal effects at high doses.
lact: It is not known whether teriparatide is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects on the breastfed infant, it is not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in mild to moderate renal impairment; clearance is reduced. Teriparatide is contraindicated/not recommended in severe renal impairment. Monitor calcium closely.
hepatic: Specific data in hepatic impairment are limited. Use with caution and individualise; teriparatide is metabolised peripherally rather than hepatically to a major extent.

major: Digoxin - teriparatide-induced transient hypercalcemia can predispose to digitalis toxicity; monitor
moderate: Other agents causing hypercalcemia (thiazides, vitamin D/calcium excess) - additive risk of hypercalcemia
minor: No clinically significant minor interactions established
interactions.food: No significant food interaction; maintain adequate calcium and vitamin D intake
interactions.alcohol: No specific drug interaction; chronic heavy alcohol use itself worsens osteoporosis
interactions.diagnostics: Transient post-dose rises in serum calcium peak about 4-6 hours after injection and normalise by 16-24 hours - sample timing affects calcium results

common: Dizziness and transient orthostatic hypotension after dosing
serious: Symptomatic orthostatic hypotension / syncope after early doses
rare: Osteosarcoma (seen in rats at high doses; the basis of historical use limits and the boxed warning for PTH products)

monitoring: Serum calcium (avoid persistent hypercalcemia); recheck if symptoms occur
Urinary calcium in patients with prior urolithiasis
Orthostatic blood pressure for the first several doses
Bone mineral density to assess treatment response
Total lifetime treatment duration (generally not beyond 24 months)
counsel: Inject under the skin of the thigh or abdomen once a day, and take the first few doses where you can sit or lie down if you feel dizzy
Keep taking your calcium and vitamin D as advised
Report ongoing nausea, vomiting, constipation, confusion, or feeling faint
Store the pen in the refrigerator and never share it with anyone else
Treatment is for a limited time (usually up to 24 months in a lifetime) - do not exceed it
pk: Bone-formation markers rise within weeks; BMD gains over months
Serum concentration peaks approximately 30 minutes after SC dose; serum calcium peaks 4-6 hours after dose
Approximately 1 hour after subcutaneous injection (about 5 minutes IV)
Brief systemic exposure; daily dosing required for the anabolic effect
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light; use pen within labeled in-use period
pearls: Recombinant human PTH(1-34) is teriparatide; full-length recombinant PTH(1-84) (Natpara) is used for hypoparathyroidism and carries an osteosarcoma boxed warning - know which product is intended
Intermittent (once-daily) PTH builds bone, whereas continuous PTH elevation (hyperparathyroidism) is catabolic - the dosing schedule is essential to the anabolic effect
Hypercalcemia is the principal metabolic adverse effect; check calcium and avoid in patients with pre-existing hypercalcemia
Take the first doses sitting or lying down because transient orthostatic hypotension can occur shortly after injection
Follow anabolic therapy with an antiresorptive agent (e.g., a bisphosphonate) to preserve BMD gains after stopping
missed: If you miss your daily injection, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Do not take two injections in one day to make up for a missed dose. Resume your normal once-daily schedule the next day.
overdose: Overdose may cause hypercalcemia (nausea, vomiting, weakness, dizziness) and orthostatic hypotension. Management is to stop the drug, monitor serum calcium, give supportive care with hydration, and treat symptomatic hypercalcemia. Because the half-life is short, effects are generally transient.
